doc.title: Pete Candoli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999

title: Bitten by his dog and bodybuilding
summary: Pete recounts his scotty biting his lip and his weight-lifting habits.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: In all the playing you’ve done, did you ever have any physical problems that kind of put a crimp in your activities for a while?

Only one time with Woody’s band. I had a scotty that used to travel with me all the time, my little scotty. And one night I came home from the Sherman Hotel and the little scotty was asleep on the bed and I guess I awakened it and it snapped unconsciously, and bit me right on the lip. So of course it bled and swelled up a little bit, but I said well I’d better cool it and bask in the sun at least for a few days or something, which we did. But they wrote a big deal about it, like “bitten on the lip by such and such.” But I used to work out all the time in Sid Klein’s gym in New York and I was a health nut to be honest with you. Then at one time I think I weighed about 225 and looked about four foot high because I wore a 46 coat. I figured that was it, I was young, I was really into it. Then it dawned upon me later, a little more sensibly, like all your energy and strength is internal really, not the big bulging muscles. Those give you the energy, the strength. So I started with more repetitions with lighter weights for more definition. But it’s true.
You probably could have won the body building contest, at least within the musician community.
I probably could have done that very easily. They put me on the cover of “Bernard.”
